issues.description: The problem statement (UML and textual description) specifies acceptSupplyDelivery should take four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity), but the provided Main example and the solution implementation of SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery use a three-parameter signature (ingredient name, price, quantity). This inconsistency will confuse students about the correct method signature to implement and may cause mismatches with example usage or tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the signature consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update problem_statement.md (UML and text) to specify acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and remove the supplier parameter, or (B) change the solution and template example to implement and call acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity). Ensure all examples, tests, and the UML match the chosen signature.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and textual description) specifies SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery with four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity) i.e., acceptSupplyDelivery(String, String, int, int). The solution implementation defines a static acceptSupplyDelivery method with three parameters (ingredient name, price, quantity) i.e., acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int). This mismatch in parameter count and conceptual parameter (missing supplier name) creates confusion for students about the expected method signature and how to map the problem requirements to the implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the signature consistent. Either: (A) update the solution to implement the four-parameter signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and (if supplier is not used) accept the supplier parameter without side-effects, or (B) revise the problem statement/UML to require three parameters (ingredientName, price, quantity). Prefer (A) to match the described requirement: add the supplierName parameter to the implementation and adjust any references accordingly.
